$comment: Cited orb and strength conventions from William Lilly's Christian Astrology (1647), for issue #590. Every passage was read from the page image of the Wellcome Library scan (archive.org b30338724), not from its OCR text. Machine-readable; one passage per object. Nothing here is corpus text.

lilly-christian-astrology-1647.title: Christian Astrology, modestly treated of in three books
lilly-christian-astrology-1647.author: William Lilly
lilly-christian-astrology-1647.edition_used: First edition, Wellcome Library copy, archive.org item b30338724
lilly-christian-astrology-1647.text_quality: page images read directly; transcribed here with the long s and ligatures resolved. Page numbers are the printed folio numbers of Book I, 'An Introduction to Astrologie'.

passages.locator: Book I, p. 107 (PDF leaf 141), 'the Table of the quantity of their Orbs'
passages.text: A Platick Aspect is that which admits of the Orbs or Rayes of two Planets that signifie any matter... they stand thus as I have found by the best Authors and my owne Experience.
passages.marginalNote: I sometimes use the one, and sometimes the other, as my Memory best remembereth them, and this without error.
passages.notes: Lilly gives two sets and says he uses either. The Moon's 12 deg 30 min first-column value is read from the image. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto are not in Lilly (undiscovered).

passages.text: As if Venus be in the tenth degree of Taurus, and Saturn in eighteen degrees of Virgo, here Venus hath a Platick Trine, or is in a Platick Trine to Saturn, because she is within the moity of both their Orbs; for the moity of Saturn his Rayes or Orbs is five, and of Venus 4, and the distance betwixt them and their perfect aspect is eight degrees.
passages.notes: Saturn's 5 and Venus's 4 are half of 10 and 8, the first-column orbs. A pair is in orb when their separation from the exact aspect is within the SUM of their moieties (here 9).

passages.topic: moiety used for application and separation
passages.text: for every Planet that applies is allowed halfe his owne orbs and halfe the orbs of that Planet from whom he seperates: As if the Sun and Moon be in any aspect, the Moon shall then be seperated from the Sun, when she is fully distant from the Sun 7 degr. and 30 min. viz. half the orbs of the Sun, and 6 degr. the moity of her owne orbes; in all 13 degr. and 30 minutes.
passages.notes: Uses the second column (Sun 15, Moon 12). The same page's Saturn/Jupiter example uses 9 and 9, each half 4 deg 30 min, summing to 9.

passages.text: A Planet is said to be Combust of the Sun, when in the same Signe where the Sun is in, he is not distant from the Sun eight degrees and thirty minutes, either before or after the Sun... I allow the moyity of his owne Orbs to shew the time of combustion, and not of Jupiter; for by that rule Jupiter should not be combust before he is within foure degrees and a half of the Sun. I know many are against this opinion.
passages.notes: Lilly states 8 deg 30 min, and records his own alternative of using the planet's own moiety, which he knows others reject. Adopted by Astraya in sect.ts: combustion within 8°30′ and in the same sign only.

passages.text: A Planet is said to be still under the Sun-beames, untill he is fully elongated or distant from his body 17 degr. either before or after him. / A Planet is in the heart of the Sunne, or in Cazimi, when he is not removed from him 17 min. or is within 17 min. forward or backward.
passages.notes: Book II (1647 vol. 2, p. 300, aphorism 26) gives different figures, 12 degrees and 16 minutes; see lilly-ii-aphorism-26. Adopted by Astraya in sect.ts: under the beams within 17°.

passages.locator: Book I, p. 115 (PDF leaf 149), 'A ready Table whereby to examine the Fortitudes and Debilities of the Planets'
passages.text: In his owne house, or in mutuall reception with another Planet by house: 5. In his exaltation, or reception by exaltation: 4. In his owne Triplicity: 3. In his owne Terme: 2. Decanate or Face: 1. Debilities: in his Detriment 5, in his Fall 4, Peregrine 5.
passages.notes: The weights are shown as 5/4/3/2/1. On the debility side the table prints 5, 4, 5 without minus signs; they are subtracted. Accidental fortitudes on the same page are not transcribed here.

passages.text: When either 00. degrees, or the first or second degrees of a Signe ascend (especially in Signes of short ascensions...) you may not adventure judgment, unlesse the Querent be very young... If 27, 28, or 29 degrees ascend of any Signe, it's no wayes safe to give judgment, except the Querent be in yeers corresponding to the number of degrees ascending...
passages.notes: Source for horary.ts's 3 and 27 degree limits. This is the section 'Considerations before Judgment' at the end of Book I (pp. 121-123); it is not in Book II, and horary.ts's 'ch. XXXVI' does not match it.

passages.text: It's not safe to judge when the Moon is in the later degrees of a Signe, especially in Gemini, Scorpio or Capricorn; or as some say, when she is in Via Combusta, which is, when she is in the last 15 degrees of Libra, or the first fifteen degrees of Scorpio. / All manner of matters goe hardly on (except the principall significators be very strong) when the Moon is voyd of course; yet somewhat she performes if voyd of course, and be either in Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius or Pisces.
passages.notes: Lilly softens void-of-course for the Moon in Taurus, Cancer, Sagittarius or Pisces. horary.ts models this: the caution still applies but does not make the chart not radical. The Via Combusta is 'as some say'.

passages.topic: considerations before judgment: the Moon in the later degrees of a sign
passages.locator: Book I, p. 122 (PDF leaf 156), the first clause of the sentence quoted in lilly-i-via-combusta-void-of-course
passages.text: It's not safe to judge when the Moon is in the later degrees of a Signe, especially in Gemini, Scorpio or Capricorn...
passages.notes: Lilly gives NO number for 'the later degrees'. The 1647 Book I and Book II, and the Houlding edition's notes, were searched; the only other uses of 'later degrees' concern moles on the body (p. 119) and a disease changing when 28 degrees of a common sign lie on the sixth cusp (Vol. 2 p. 268), and neither says what counts as later for the Moon. For the Ascendant he does give numbers (27, 28 or 29 degrees), but he does not say the Moon uses them. 'Especially in Gemini, Scorpio or Capricorn' is a qualifier: the caution is stated for any sign. Not implemented; see the decision 'moon in the later degrees'.

passages.topic: Moon void of course, and where it matters less
passages.locator: Book II, p. 299 (aphorism 9), PDF leaf 333 of the Wellcome scan
passages.text: Generally consider the state of the Moon, for if she be void of course there's no great hopes of the Question propounded, that it shall be effected; yet if she be in Cancer, Taurus, Sagittarius or Pisces, your fear may be lesse, for then she is not much impedited by being voyd of course.
passages.notes: Agrees with Book I p. 122, which names the same four signs in a different order.

passages.topic: under the beams and cazimi, the Book II aphorism
passages.locator: Book II, p. 300 (aphorism 26), PDF leaf 334 of the Wellcome scan
passages.text: A Planet within twelve degrees of the Sun, is said to be under his Beames, and then hath no fortitude, let it be in what Signe it will; when a Planet is within sixteen minutes of the Sun, he is said to be in Cazimi, or heat of the Sun, and then it's an addition of fortune, and he is wonderous strong.
passages.notes: Read from the page image of the 1647 Wellcome scan (archive.org b30338724, leaf 334); it matches the web transcription of Book II. It conflicts with Book I p. 113 (17 degrees, 17 minutes); both are Lilly's, and Book I is followed. Lilly writes the numbers out ('twelve', 'sixteen').

decisions.decision: Offer the two columns of Lilly's table as two presets, 'Lilly, first column' and 'Lilly, second column', as per-body moieties (half the orb). The Standard, Tight and Wide profiles stay Astraya defaults.
Lilly predates Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, so his presets carry no orb for them; a pair with one missing body falls back to the aspect's own tier.

Book I's figures are adopted: combustion within 8°30′ in the same sign, under the beams within 17°, cazimi within 17′. Book II's aphorism (12°, 16′) is recorded but not followed, because Book I is the fuller statement and matches the cazimi value.

Not checked. Lilly names the caution but gives no threshold, and Astraya does not invent one: borrowing the Ascendant's 27 degrees would present a guess as his rule. The horary screen therefore does not flag it, and a chart with the Moon at the end of a sign can read as fit to be judged. If a source with a threshold is found, add it here first, then to horary.ts.
